_README: OUR weights, not Hoberman's. Hoberman's Data Model Scorecard (SRC-HOB-SC) totals
100 across ten categories, but the per-category allocation is published only
inside the book and could not be verified during authoring. These numbers are a
defensible default we chose; they are not the published scorecard. Never present
them as Hoberman's in a report — say 'weighted with our allocation' and point at
this file.
Tune them for a given engagement rather than arguing about them: a greenfield
design review should weight Abstraction and Definitions higher, a pre-load
readiness review should weight Structure and Data higher.
Categories listed in REQUIRES_EXTERNAL_INPUT (rules.py) are dropped from the
denominator when their input is absent, rather than scored zero. A model must not
lose points because the reviewer did not have a requirements document.
Points deducted from a category per finding, before the category floor at 0.
BLOCKER is deliberately steep: one finding that loses data should visibly move
the number, because a scorecard that averages a data-loss defect into
insignificance is worse than no scorecard.
Repeat findings of the same rule in one category are damped (see
score_model.py REPEAT_DAMPING) so that a single systemic issue across 200
tables does not zero every category on its own.
Nth occurrence of the same rule contributes penalty * damping^(n-1).
Set to 1.0 to disable damping and let volume dominate.
Tier-B (judged) dimensions are reported as a band, not a decimal, because a
reviewer's judgement does not carry three significant figures. These are the
point values a band contributes when it is mapped into the numeric scorecard,
expressed as a fraction of the category weight retained.

grade_scale._README: Reported alongside the number so a percentage is not read as precision.
grade_scale.90: Exemplary — would use as a reference model
grade_scale.75: Sound — defects are localised and cheap to fix
grade_scale.60: Workable — real rework needed before it carries production data
grade_scale.0: Not fit for purpose as designed
